newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: S.Africa plans roadshow for Samurai issue in June.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa plans roadshow for Samurai issue in June.

text.p: South Afica will hold a roadshow in Toyko early next month for its planned Samurai yen bond issue, the country's Director General of Finance, Maria Ramos, said on Thursday.

"It will be a short, three-day roadshow. We haven't been to that market since 1995 so it is also a time to report back and touch base with investors," she told reporters at an investment conference in Harare.

The government was still assessing the situation regarding its planned Yankee dollar bond issue, she added, following the decision by the U.S. Federal Reserve not to push up interest rates at its meeting this week.
"We are looking at how the market is going to settle, at what the opportunities look like and we will decide over the next couple of weeks what we are going to do on that front."
No roadshow has yet been planned for the Yankee issue.
South Africa has already awarded the mandate for the Samurai issue to Daiwa Securities while Merrill Lynch will lead manage the Yankee bond.
The 1997/98 (April-March) budget targets the raising of four billion road in foreign bond markets this year and Ramos said she expected the Samurai and Yankee issues to meet this target between them.
The government has not yet decided how much to raise with each bond, she added.
